overview.text: Renewables, including large hydro, supplied 24.9% of India's gross electricity generation (1,961 TWh in total). Adding nuclear, non-fossil sources supplied 28.0%; coal and lignite alone supplied 70.7%.
Peak demand met reached 270.8 GW on 21 May 2026.

mix.text: The renewable share was highest in Aug 2026 (31.5%) and lowest in Dec 2025 (19.9%): a swing of 11.6 percentage points within one year.
mix.caveat: Seasonal pattern from a single year; not a multi-year trend.

mix.text: North-Eastern region had the highest renewable share (50.2%); Eastern had the lowest (6.0%).
On the peak-demand day (2026-05-21), solar produced 80 GW at 12:30 but 0 GW at 19:30; thermal output rose from 141 GW to 182 GW to cover the evening.
mix.caveat: SCADA data can contain telemetry errors.

mix.text: Coal stations generated 4.5% less than CEA's programme for the year; hydro was 8.1% below programme.

renewables.text: Capacity factors over the year: solar 24.1%, wind 27.8%, large hydro 31.7%, coal 68.3%, nuclear 78.6%. Solar and wind run below thermal plants because sun and wind are not always available, not because the plants fail.
renewables.source: CEA Daily Generation Reports; CEA Daily Renewable Generation Reports
renewables.caveat: Solar and wind capacity factors use inter-state (ISGS) stations only; net generation.

renewables.text: Wind is the most seasonal source: in its best month (Jul 2026) it produced 4.2x as much per day as in its weakest (Nov 2025).
Daily wind and solar output are positively correlated (r = 0.12). Day-to-day variation of wind and solar combined is 24.9% (coefficient of variation), versus 61.5% for wind and 16.1% for solar alone.
Rajasthan generated 35.4% of India's reported solar output.
renewables.caveat: Reported grid-connected generation; rooftop solar is not included.

renewables.text: Gujarat generated 35.5% of India's reported wind output.
renewables.caveat: Reported grid-connected generation; rooftop solar is not included.

outages.text: Average share of capacity unavailable over the year: coal 15.7%, lignite 28.9%, gas 52.0%, nuclear 17.5%, large hydro 19.5%. Gas lost the largest share.
outages.caveat: Gas plants are often idle for lack of gas or schedule; that is reported as outage too.

outages.text: Of the coal, lignite and nuclear capacity out on an average day (38.3 GW), 55% was down for equipment failures and 19% for fuel or commercial reasons rather than breakdowns.

5,404 equipment-failure outages started during the year across 628 units. The most common cause was 'water wall tube leakage' (860 events). Median repair time for failures with a reported return was 29 hours.
outages.caveat: Durations only for outages whose return time was reported.

outages.text: 20 units (815 MW) had been out for more than a year before the window started and were still out at its end (no fuel agreement, awaiting scrapping, reserve shutdown).
MUNDRA UMTPP (Gujarat) lost the most capacity to equipment failures: 730,400 MW-days.
Solar and wind: on an average day 5.9% of monitored solar capacity (6.1 GW) and 5.8% of wind capacity (3.1 GW) was not available, against 15.7% for coal.
outages.caveat: Installed minus the day's maximum available capacity; a different measure from CEA's capacity under outage for thermal plants, so compare with care.

outages.text: 112 of the 521 grid disturbances in the year took solar, wind or other renewable plants offline, losing 38,719 MW of generation in total. The largest (Rajasthan, 2026-01-14) cut 3,787 MW.
outages.caveat: Most of these are trips of the line or substation that carries the plant's power, not plant faults.

outages.text: Inter-state solar stations reported zero output on 2,112 station-days (2.9% of all station-days), in 740 episodes across 119 stations; the median episode lasted 1 day(s).
outages.caveat: A proxy: a zero day can also be a reporting error. Stations that report zero on over 90% of days are excluded.

supply.text: Unmet demand totalled 1,675 MU, 0.09% of demand. Punjab had the most (417 MU).
supply.caveat: Unmet demand reported by states. It is not a measure of household power cuts.

supply.text: Month by month, average generation outage and unmet demand have a correlation of r = -0.57.
supply.caveat: Correlation, not causation: a plant outage does not by itself cause a consumer power cut.
